relevance_note: Case report of a patient and relatives carrying a TNFAIP3 variant: "A heterozygous mutation of TNFAIP3 (c.305A>G, p. Asn 102 Ser) was identified in the patient."
method_note: Read the whole paper manually (case report, no tables, no supplementary section); a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans. In scope: the proband ('patient'), her father and brother (both carry the identical TNFAIP3 variant), and her pregnant sister, who was tested and lacked the variant (row kept as a tested-negative relative; no variant row). 'Other family members without TNFAIP3 mutation' (Sanger of the 'whole genealogy', Western blot) are not individually described and get no rows; the mother is never mentioned. Inheritance left 'not reported' for all carriers: the father carries the identical variant, but the paper never states that the patient or brother inherited it from him. Variant class left 'not reported': the authors call it a 'heterozygous deleterious mutation' but never name the class. STRA8 and UEVLD: the paper attributes 'two homozygous deleterious mutations' to the patient's WES and dismisses them; read as one variant per gene, recorded with variant_original_string 'not reported' because details are only in Figure 2B. The functional statement includes a cited (ref 10) sentence beginning 'This mutation causes decreased A20 expression...'; it is not fully clear whether 'This mutation' means c.305A>G specifically or TNFAIP3 mutations generally. Tension in the paper: the variant is called 'novel' and 'not been previously reported in HA20', yet the paper lists population frequencies (e.g. MAF=0.0135 in GnomAD_EAS, 0.01734 in ExAC) and cites refs 10-12 for this mutation as a functional SNP/risk factor. Sister's lower A20 expression is a laboratory finding without a TNFAIP3 variant and is not recorded as a phenotypic feature. Low-titre ANA (1:100) recorded as observed for the autoantibody checklist item, as printed. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper makes no statement either way. No contradictions about any person's features were found.
